assign.request: Audit today's work: every request the owner made in their own words beside what was done, with a verdict judged against their sentence; an approval process that persists (Approve / Needs work per card); how the AI pages' data is stored and loaded with a split recommendation and a measured threshold; and where the Live toggle stands plus how new cards really arrive.

steps: Extract the owner's words from the board and the mastermind inbox
Map today's task dirs to what each one landed

PROOF-OF-STREAM: this line was appended while a headless browser had this page open, to settle whether a new card arrives over the socket or through a live reload.

Sources read. The owner's verbatim words are 48 cards on ai/v/3/board.jsonl (author: owner, 15:44 to 17:21) plus 5 earlier relay lines in the mastermind's inbox - 53 distinct prompts. The mastermind's own ledger records exactly 53 asks for today, so the two agree on the count.

Finding: the ledger's per-ask 'quote' field is often the mastermind's own paraphrase written in the third person, not the owner's words. This audit reads the owner's words from board.jsonl instead and attaches them to 30 of the 53 items by time proximity.
Verdicts, judged against the owner's sentence rather than each task's landing report: 30 done as asked, 12 partly, 5 done but differs, 6 not done. 53 total.

Top finding: ask 'joint-timeline' is recorded as LANDED and its conclusion is a promise - 'one joint timeline is being built'. The task that would build it, ai/2026-09-19/v3-timeline/, has requirements.md and NO task.jsonl, which means no agent was ever dispatched. The same brief holds the timeline grid, the toolbar and the Live toggle.

Second finding: the V3 layout ask is recorded landed at 16:25; the owner said it was still wrong at 16:27, 16:39, 16:49, 17:08 and 17:17 ('We still do not have the proper layout that I asked for'). Full bleed, two EQUAL columns and the left timeline with hour lines are all still missing.

decision.title: Approvals ride the dev server's existing rpc:append - no Server/ change needed
decision.text: Verified the mastermind's call: ai/v/3/timeline.js merges card lines by id (card(), lines 43-48), so an approval is one more line. The browser write path already exists: Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js accepts any .jsonl under public/ and appends one whole line with mode 'a', so two writers interleave between lines and never inside one. The page therefore writes to its own approvals.jsonl and needs nothing from Server/. CardAnswer.js (landed 17:34) is the board-specific version of the same idea and is what puts these buttons on a real board card.

log.msg: Measured: board.jsonl 155 KB / 270 lines, mastermind ledger 393 KB / 804 lines across three days, day.jsonl 13 KB, 26 task logs 304 KB total (largest 32 KB), usage.jsonl 79 KB. Today's 6 MB dir is 5.1 MB of screenshots; all the text logs together are 324 KB.

Measured parse+merge of the real board at 1x/10x/100x/400x: 0.4 ms at 155 KB, 3.3 ms at 1.5 MB, 27.8 ms at 15.5 MB, 110 ms at 62 MB. Parsing never becomes the cost. Recommendation: split board.jsonl per day at a 5 MB per-file threshold; the truly unbounded file is the mastermind ledger, which is per-run and a run has no end.

Live toggle: NOT built and never dispatched - item 7 of ai/2026-09-19/v3-timeline/requirements.md, a dir with a brief and no task.jsonl. Settled with evidence how new cards arrive: LiveReload.js line 138 routes every .jsonl change to Tail.changed() instead of the reload queue, so only the new bytes go down the socket.

Proved it headless on the private server (PORT=8094): a .jsonl append left an in-page sentinel alive and never navigated; writing an ordinary .css file reloaded the page and destroyed the sentinel. Socket stream, not live reload.

Proved the approval round trip on the same server: pressing Approve appended one line to approvals.jsonl (13 ms), both copies of the item flipped to 'approved' with no reload, and the state survived a real page reload. Zero page errors, zero failed requests, no horizontal overflow at 1440 or 400 px.

assign.outcome:
**53 things you asked for today. 30 were done the way you said them; 23 were not.** 12 partly, 5 done but different from what you said, 6 not started at all. Every verdict is judged against YOUR sentence, not against the report the task wrote about itself.

![the audit page: the counts, then the five items that need your eye, each with Approve and Needs work](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/day-audit/shot.png)

**The five worth your eye, in order:**
1. **The joint timeline is recorded as LANDED and was never built.** Its own conclusion is a promise — "one joint timeline is being built". The task that would build it, `ai/2026-09-19/v3-timeline/`, has a finished brief and **no task log at all**, which is what a dir looks like when no agent was ever sent.
2. **The V3 layout** was recorded landed at 16:25. You said it was still wrong at 16:27, 16:39, 16:49, 17:08 and 17:17 — "We still do not have the proper layout that I asked for." Full bleed, two *equal* columns and the left timeline with hour lines are all still missing.
3. **The Live toggle does not exist and nobody was sent to build it** — it is item 7 of that same undispatched brief, along with the toolbar you asked for twice.
4. **The verbatim relay hook is built, tested, and switched OFF.** Your words reached the board today because a Sonnet session remembered to send them, not because the machine did. One settings line from you turns it on.
5. **"Never break the page" did not hold.** The alarm and the auditor landed; the site still went down twice more — `tree.js` at 14:51 and 15:05, and a bad import in `compose.js` blanked everything for about 80 seconds near 17:00.

**The approval buttons persist, and nothing new was invented.** Your decision is one more append-only line merged by `id` — the exact rule the board already uses (`ai/v/3/timeline.js`, `card()`). The write path already existed too: the dev server's `rpc:append` takes one line at a time, so two writers interleave between lines and never inside one. **No `Server/` change was needed.** Proved headless: a press appended the line in 13 ms, both copies of the item flipped with no reload, and the state survived a real page reload — zero errors, no overflow at 400 px.

**New cards arrive over the socket. There is no reload involved.** `LiveReload.js` line 138 sends every `.jsonl` change to `Tail.changed()` instead of the reload queue. Proved both ways on a private server: appending a `.jsonl` line left an in-page marker alive and never navigated; writing an ordinary `.css` file reloaded the page and destroyed it.

**Splitting the logs: one file per day for the board, at a 5 MB threshold.** Parsing is never the cost — the real board parses and merges in 0.4 ms, and even at 62 MB it is only 110 ms. Loading a whole day is free, exactly as you guessed. The one file genuinely growing without a bound is the **mastermind's own ledger** (393 KB across three days, because a "run" has no end) — that one matters more than the board.

**Left, on purpose:** the approvals live in this task's own `approvals.jsonl` rather than on the board, because `ai/v/3/**` is another minion's page this week; moving them is a copy, since the line shape is already the board's. The audit judges 53 requests; ten of the most important landings were checked against the actual files (`framework.css`'s `.card`, the two renamed skills, `v3.css`, the two undispatched dirs), the rest against the record.
